thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: p99 latency breach detected on /v1/generate (streaming) — suspected preproc/tokenizer slowdown. Incident ID INC-3190. Paging: @maya.nguyen @liam.hendrix @kai @emily.sre. See dashboards: https://dash.company/INC-3190

maya.nguyen: I'm on pager. starting triage — grabbing p95/p99 graphs and preproc traces now.

liam.hendrix: I can take request sampling + router logs. If this is template expansion or JSON-mode it's likely CPU-bound in preproc.

kai: Quick note: streaming tail latency is spiking ~45s p99 for some requests, users seeing stalled tokens. p95 ~620ms, p99 ~45,000ms.

emily.sre: copy. Are errors increasing or just latency?

support-jen: We've got 9 open customer tickets calling out "stalled responses" and 3 enterprise customers paged us via CSE. CS says one customer saw multiple streaming stalls in the last 5m.

maya.nguyen: Looking at preproc-host CPU: sustained 95% on a subset of hosts. Tokenizer process (preproc) shows long GC pauses on a couple of nodes.

liam.hendrix: Request samples show large prompt templates with heavy tool schema assembly + JSON-mode parsing. Example request snippet:```json
{"prompt_template":"{{tools}} call","tools":[{"schema":{...large...}}],"mode":"json"}```That explains heavy CPU on template rendering + JSON validation.

kai: Also seeing KV cache warmup not the issue — this happens before model tokens are emitted (so pre-tokenizer). Streaming stalls start right after preproc returns.

maya.nguyen: Immediate mitigation proposals: 1) Route streaming traffic to fallback route that disables JSON-mode validation for non-enterprise requests. 2) Scale preproc autoscaling group + restart overloaded preproc workers to recover GC. 3) Apply a temporary rate-limit on very large template/tool-schema requests. Thoughts?

emily.sre: Do 1 and 2 in parallel. Rolling restart of preproc pool should be gradual (canary then bulk). I'll coordinate.

devex-alex: For customers that need JSON-mode we should keep a canary path with stricter CPU limit. But for now disabling JSON-mode for new requests will reduce validation overhead. We can fallback to tolerant-parser mode that returns structured but less strict output.

liam.hendrix: I'll push router policy to send traffic with header `x-allow-jsonmode: false` for default route, and add a /json-mode-special route for whitelisted enterprise. Command:```bash
rb-router update-policy --route /v1/generate --set header:x-allow-jsonmode=false --dry-run=false```

ops-bot: Executed: rb-router update-policy ... - result: success on 6/6 control planes.

maya.nguyen: Rolling restart started: restarting preproc-worker pool on region-a (canary 2 nodes).

kai: Metrics update 2m in: p95 down to 580ms, p99 down to 3.2s on canary traffic. Good signal.

support-jen: CS update: two of the enterprise customers still experiencing stalls (they're likely whitelisted for JSON-mode). Reached out to offer temporary routing to fallback model.

maya.nguyen: Restart finished for region-a, rolling to region-b. Also applied temporary threshold: reject templates >2MB with 413 and link to decomp docs.

liam.hendrix: Found a pathological case: nested tool-schema arrays causing exponential template rendering time when combined with certain handlebars helpers. Filed bug: PREPROC-427.

devex-alex: Can we add a quick mitigation in frontend: rewrite complex tool schemas into references before sending to preproc? Maybe add a preflight that hashes large schemas and refers to stored attachments.

emily.sre: For incident postmortem action items: - PREPROC-427 triage/root cause, - Router policy changes rollback plan, - Add preflight size-limits + better client errors, - Improve monitoring for template expansion CPU.

support-jen: Customer impact: ~12 active customers affected, 3 enterprise with high throughput. Estimated user-facing error rate spike: 22 errors/min at peak. We should offer credits for impacted customers — CS drafting emails.

kai: Final metrics after 10m: p95 430ms, p99 1.8s, streaming stall reports reduced to baseline. Keeping incident open for monitoring for 30m.

maya.nguyen: Confirming live mitigations: router policy change deployed, preproc pool restarted (gradual), large-template rejects enabled, temporary JSON-mode whitelist active. I'm going to hand off to emily.sre for postmortem.

emily.sre: Taking handoff. I'll open INC-3190 in incident tracker and coordinate postmortem. Thanks all — please add relevant logs/traces to the ticket (link: https://incidents/INC-3190). :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-3190 acknowledged and set to monitoring state. Next update in 30m or on regression.
